Interface RandomSelector<T>

Type Parameters:
T - the type of the elements
All Known Implementing Classes:
MutableRandomSelector
Functional Interface:
This is a functional interface and can therefore be used as the assignment target for a lambda expression or method reference.
@FunctionalInterface public interface RandomSelector<T>
Selects an element at random, each time it's asked to, with the source of randomness it's given. 
var rarity = RandomSelector.weighted(Maps.map("common", 70, "rare", 25, "legendary", 5));
rarity.next(random);                         // "common", 70% of the time
rarity.stream(random).limit(10).toList();

var monster = RandomSelector.weighted(bestiary, Monster::frequency);
var card = RandomSelector.uniform(deck);

A weighted selection takes the same time whatever the number of elements: the weights are turned once into a table of as many slots as there are elements, each shared between at most two of them, and a selection takes a slot, then one of its two elements, with a single call to RandomGenerator.nextLong().

Selectors are combined into other selectors. flatten(RandomSelector) selects a selector, then an element from it, which is how a table of elements refers to other tables: 

var gems = RandomSelector.weighted(Maps.map(ruby, 3, diamond, 1));
var weapons = RandomSelector.uniform(List.of(sword, axe, bow));
var chest = RandomSelector.flatten(
        RandomSelector.weighted(Maps.map(gems, 30, weapons, 10, RandomSelector.constant(gold), 60)));

This is a functional interface: any function of a RandomGenerator is a selector, such as random -> random.nextInt(1, 7). The selectors that this interface creates are immutable, keep a copy of their elements, and may be shared between threads if the source of randomness given to them may.

Since:
0.2.0

    • chances

      default Chances<T> chances()
      Returns the exact chance of each element that this selector selects.

      The selectors that this interface creates know their chances, and so do those made from them with map(Function) and flatten(RandomSelector). A selector that is a function of a RandomGenerator doesn't, unless it overrides this method.

      Returns:
      the chances of the elements
      Throws:
      UnsupportedOperationException - if this selector doesn't know its chances

    • uniform

      static <T> RandomSelector<T> uniform(Collection<? extends T> elements)
      Returns a selector that selects each element of a collection with the same chance. An element that occurs several times in the collection has as many chances to be selected.

      Each selection calls nextInt(size) once, and selects the element at that index in the iteration order of the collection. A selector of one element uses no randomness.

      Type Parameters:
      T - the type of the elements
      Parameters:
      elements - the elements to select from
      Returns:
      a selector of the elements
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if elements is empty

    • weighted

      static <T> RandomSelector<T> weighted(Collection<? extends T> elements, ToDoubleFunction<? super T> weight)
      Returns a selector that selects each element of a collection with a chance proportional to its weight. An element whose weight is zero is never selected.

      Each selection calls RandomGenerator.nextLong() once. Which element a given number selects isn't specified, only how often each element is selected. When the positive weights are all equal, the selector is the uniform one of their elements, and calls what it calls.

      Type Parameters:
      T - the type of the elements
      Parameters:
      elements - the elements to select from
      weight - the function that gives the weight of an element
      Returns:
      a selector of the elements
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if a weight is negative, infinite or not a number, if their sum is infinite, or if no element has a positive weight

    • weighted

      static <T> RandomSelector<T> weighted(Map<? extends T, ? extends Number> weights)
      Returns a selector that selects each key of a map with a chance proportional to its value. A key whose weight is zero is never selected.

      Which element a given source of randomness selects depends on the order of the map: for selections that are the same from one run to the next, with a seeded source, use a map with a defined order.

      Each selection calls RandomGenerator.nextLong() once. Which element a given number selects isn't specified, only how often each element is selected. When the positive weights are all equal, the selector is the uniform one of their elements, and calls what it calls.

      Type Parameters:
      T - the type of the elements
      Parameters:
      weights - the weights of the elements to select from
      Returns:
      a selector of the elements
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if a weight is negative, infinite or not a number, if their sum is infinite, or if no element has a positive weight

    • flatten

      static <T> RandomSelector<T> flatten(RandomSelector<? extends RandomSelector<? extends T>> selectors)
      Returns a selector that selects a selector, then an element from it. Each selection uses the randomness of both, in that order.
      Type Parameters:
